Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked to brown spots on leaves; fruit spots can become raised and scabby. Heavy infection causes leaf drop and sunscald.
organic_treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves and plant debris.
Use drip irrigation and avoid working plants when leaves are wet.
chemical_treatment: Copper sprays used preventively where allowed; resistance can occur.
In many areas copper is mixed with mancozeb or used with Actigard (plant defence activator) - follow local labels.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed/transplants.
Rotate crops (avoid pepper/tomato in same spot for 2-3 years).
Disinfect tools and avoid handling wet plants.
Use resistant/tolerant varieties where available.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.notes: Warm, wet weather favours this disease. Streptomycin is not recommended for field use in most regions.

Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: No obvious disease symptoms in the image.
prevention: Keep watering even and nutrition balanced.
Check plants regularly for spots, yellowing or pests.
Give plants good spacing and airflow.
Pepper__bell___healthy.notes: Healthy in the image does not guarantee the whole plant is problem-free.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings, usually on older lower leaves. Spots are dry and can join together.
organic_treatment: Remove badly infected lower leaves and debris.
Mulch to reduce soil splash and keep leaves drier.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered fungicide for early blight when needed.
Rotate fungicide types to slow resistance.
prevention: Rotate crops (avoid potato/tomato in same spot for 2-3 years).
Keep plants well fed and watered; avoid nitrogen deficiency.
Space plants for good airflow.
Clear crop debris after harvest.
Potato___Early_blight.notes: Adequate nitrogen reduces early blight severity by delaying leaf ageing.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Fast-spreading dark, water-soaked lesions; white mould may appear under leaves in humid weather. Tubers can rot.
organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering and improve airflow.
chemical_treatment: Use a late-blight specific fungicide as soon as disease is suspected.
Follow local resistance advice; do not rely only on metalaxyl/mefenoxam.
prevention: Watch closely in cool, wet weather.
Remove volunteer potato/tomato plants nearby.
Plant healthy seed and hill soil over tubers.
Use local late-blight warnings if available.
Potato___Late_blight.notes: This disease can destroy a crop in days. Treat any positive sign as urgent.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No obvious disease symptoms in the image.
prevention: Keep nutrition balanced and watering consistent.
Scout regularly, especially after cool wet spells.
Rotate crops and use healthy seed tubers.
Potato___healthy.notes: Healthy in the image does not rule out hidden or early infections.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark spots on leaves and stems; fruit spots can be raised and scabby. Severe infection causes leaf drop.
organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
Avoid overhead irrigation and working plants when wet.
chemical_treatment: Copper sprays used preventively where allowed; resistance can occur.
Often used with mancozeb or Actigard - follow local labels.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed/transplants.
Rotate crops and disinfect tools.
Avoid handling wet plants.
Use resistant/tolerant varieties where available.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.notes: Looks similar to some fungal leaf spots; lab/extension diagnosis may be needed in serious outbreaks.

Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with target-like rings on older leaves, often with yellow around them. Leaves turn yellow and drop over time.
organic_treatment: Remove infected lower leaves and debris.
Mulch and water at the base to keep leaves drier.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered fungicide when needed.
Rotate fungicide types to manage resistance.
prevention: Stake/cage plants for airflow.
Rotate crops and clear debris after harvest.
Keep nutrition balanced; avoid low nitrogen.
Water at the base, not overhead.
Tomato_Early_blight.notes: Often confused with late blight and target spot; rapid, water-soaked lesions need urgent late-blight action.

Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Fast-spreading dark, water-soaked lesions; white mould may appear under leaves in humid weather. Fruit can develop firm brown patches.
organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering and improve airflow.
chemical_treatment: Use a late-blight specific fungicide as soon as disease is suspected.
Follow local resistance advice; do not rely only on metalaxyl/mefenoxam.
prevention: Watch closely in cool, wet weather.
Remove volunteer tomato/potato plants nearby.
Stake plants and avoid wetting foliage late in the day.
Use local late-blight warnings if available.
Tomato_Late_blight.notes: Can destroy a planting within days. Treat any positive sign as urgent.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on top of leaves with olive-green/grey fuzzy mould directly underneath, especially in humid greenhouses.
organic_treatment: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity.
Remove infected leaves and avoid wetting foliage late.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered fungicide if needed.
Follow label and rotate products if spraying repeatedly.
prevention: Increase spacing and prune for airflow.
Keep greenhouse humidity down and avoid leaf wetness.
Avoid overhead watering late in the day.
Use resistant varieties where available.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.notes: Fuzzy growth on the leaf underside is the key sign.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small spots with grey/tan centres and dark edges; tiny black dots may appear in the centre. Starts on lower leaves and causes heavy leaf drop.
organic_treatment: Remove infected lower leaves and debris.
Mulch and avoid overhead watering.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered fungicide when needed.
Rotate fungicide types to manage resistance.
prevention: Stake/cage plants for airflow.
Rotate crops and clear debris after harvest.
Avoid wetting leaves late in the day.
Keep good spacing between plants.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.notes: Tiny black dots in spots help distinguish it from other leaf spots.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, later bronzing and leaf drop; fine webbing on leaf undersides in heavy infestations.
organic_treatment: Spray leaves (especially undersides) with water, insecticidal soap or horticultural oil.
Use neem oil or predatory mites where available.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered miticide when needed.
Rotate miticide types to slow resistance.
prevention: Avoid drought stress; keep plants well watered.
Check leaf undersides regularly in hot weather.
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum insecticides.
Use integrated pest management, not just sprays.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.notes: This is a pest, not a disease. Fungicides will not help.

Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Larger brown spots with concentric rings that can join together and cause heavy leaf drop; stems and fruit can also be affected.
organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves and debris.
Improve airflow and avoid long periods of leaf wetness.
chemical_treatment: Use a locally registered fungicide when needed.
Rotate fungicide types to manage resistance.
prevention: Stake/cage plants and keep good spacing.
Avoid overhead watering and wet foliage late in the day.
Clear crop debris after harvest.
Use resistant/tolerant varieties where available.
Tomato__Target_Spot.notes: Can look like early blight; extension confirmation may help in bad outbreaks.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunted bushy growth, flower drop and very low fruit set, especially if infected early.
organic_treatment: No cure for the virus; remove badly infected plants.
Control whiteflies with traps, soaps/neem and reflective mulch.
chemical_treatment: Insecticides may be used against whiteflies where allowed; they do not cure infected plants.
Follow local resistance and IPM advice.
prevention: Use TYLCV-resistant varieties where available.
Protect seedlings with insect-proof netting.
Remove nearby weeds that host whiteflies.
Bag and carefully remove infected plants.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.notes: Viral diseases cannot be cured with fungicides or bactericides.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaves, leaf distortion, stunting and reduced fruit quality or set.
organic_treatment: No cure; remove badly infected plants.
Disinfect tools, hands and surfaces to stop mechanical spread.
chemical_treatment: No chemical cures this virus.
Focus on clean seed/transplants and resistant varieties.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and healthy transplants.
Use resistant varieties where available.
Disinfect tools and avoid moving sap between plants.
Remove infected plant material carefully.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.notes: This virus spreads easily by touch and contaminated tools.

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No obvious disease symptoms in the image.
prevention: Keep watering even and nutrition balanced.
Check plants regularly for spots, curling or pests.
Stake/cage plants and maintain good airflow.
Rotate crops and use healthy planting material.
Tomato_healthy.notes: Healthy in the image does not guarantee the whole plant is problem-free.
